issues.body: In `run_case`, `out="$(cd "$WORK" && $JSCPD "${TUNING[@]}" "$@" "$dir" 2>&1)"` relies on word splitting to turn the default `npx --yes jscpd@4.0.5` string into command arguments. ShellCheck reports SC2086 for this expansion. Because `.github/workflows/docs-quality.yml` runs `shellcheck scripts/tests/test_docs_duplication.sh` without an exclusion before running the fixture suite, the hard-gate job fails during static analysis. The documented `JSCPD="node …/jscpd"` override likewise depends on unsafe word splitting and pathname expansion.
issues.fix_hint: Represent the command and its fixed arguments as a Bash array and invoke it as `"${JSCPD_CMD[@]}"`. If an override is needed, accept an executable path separately rather than parsing a multi-word command string. Verify with the exact workflow ShellCheck command and then run the behavioral self-test.
issues.title: Mandatory ShellCheck still rejects the unquoted JSCPD command expansion

verdict.summary: Round 4 remains blocked by the same major finding as round 3. `run_case` still invokes the configurable multi-word `JSCPD` string through an unquoted `$JSCPD` expansion. The workflow runs ShellCheck without an exclusion before the behavioral fixtures, so SC2086 rejects the new script and prevents the hard-gate job from reaching its self-test. No material progress is visible on the prior finding.
